chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassha', from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr al-Nakhas, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).
Regarding a man who has intercourse and his garment falls off, he said: 'There is no objection (it is permissible).'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man's clothing falls off during intercourse?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if a man's garment falls off during sexual intercourse, there is no objection (*la ba'sa*), indicating that the act remains valid and does not necessitate a specific corrective ritual beyond what is already prescribed. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in marital relations, distinguishing between minor disruptions in attire and major impurities that require *ghusl*. It underscores the naturalness of physical intimacy within marriage, ensuring that minor accidents do not complicate the spiritual or legal status of the couple.
